You review a Rust program against a numbered requirement document.
For each requirement Rn, decide whether the program satisfies it on the intended
concurrency semantics: answer yes, no, or unsure, and cite the Rust line(s) that
justify your answer. Also decide whether the program contains a concurrency bug
(deadlock, lost wakeup, race, busy-wait, missing release, ...): yes, no, or
unsure, with the offending line. Do not assume the program is correct.
Output only a JSON object:
{"bug_present": "yes|no|unsure", "bug_evidence": "<line refs or ->",
 "requirements": {"R1": {"satisfied": "yes|no|unsure", "line": "<refs>"}, ...}}

content: {"bug_present": "no", "bug_evidence": "-", "requirements": {"R1": {"satisfied": "no", "line": "struct Shared { a: Mutex<()>, b: Mutex<()> } (lines 4-7); both resources owned by a single Shared struct, not two modules"}, "R2": {"satisfied": "yes", "line": "t1 (line 9) and t2 (line 15) run in separate threads (lines 28, 31) and both lock a and b"}, "R3": {"satisfied": "no", "line": "no declaration of dependency on the other module's resource; t1 and t2 both directly access shared.a and shared.b"}, "R4": {"satisfied": "yes", "line": "t1: _ga = shared.a.lock() (line 10), _gb = shared.b.lock() (line 11); t2: lines 16-17; both held simultaneously"}, "R5": {"satisfied": "yes", "line": "both t1 and t2 acquire a then b in the same order (lines 10-11, 16-17), preventing circular wait"}, "R6": {"satisfied": "yes", "line": "drop(_gb); drop(_ga); (lines 12-13, 18-19)"}, "R7": {"satisfied": "yes", "line": "h1.join().unwrap(); h2.join().unwrap(); (lines 34-35) before println"}, "R8": {"satisfied": "yes", "line": "t1 and t2 run in separate threads (lines 28, 31) and both complete before joins return"}, "R9": {"satisfied": "yes", "line": "consistent lock ordering (lines 10-11, 16-17) ensures no deadlock; all schedules terminate"}, "R10": {"satisfied": "yes", "line": "println!(\"DONE done=1\"); (line 37)"}}}
